readme: Registry of automations + critical outputs the health-heartbeat.ps1 watches for SILENT DEATH - an automation that stopped being scheduled (deleted/disabled), or an output that quietly went stale, WITHOUT a loud failure. Since 2026-08-22 health-heartbeat runs from the 'TC Grocery Capture Watchdog' task, moved to 10:30 on 2026-08-31 (the NAME still says 0930 and is deliberately not renamed - it is the key this registry and audit-script-census match on) (local-watchdog.ps1 and the SMP tasks are retired); capture-watchdog covers loud failures and the run record. Brad's rule 2026-08-22: Windows tasks are the ONLY routines that fire (no Claude scheduled agents) - every one belongs HERE, and health-heartbeat's REGISTRY DRIFT check pages if a 'TC *' or 'SMP *' task exists that is not listed. The rule was written when there were exactly three and said 'the three TC Grocery tasks'; two more were registered after it (TC Graph Nightly Matching 08-22, TC Recipe Harvest Crawl 08-24) and neither was added here, so each was unwatched from birth. Re-worded 2026-08-25 to state the rule that actually holds - a registry whose preamble contradicts its own contents teaches the reader to skip both. THE COUNT IS NOT THE RULE; THE REGISTRATION IS. Adding a task without adding it here is the defect, whatever the total. max_age_hours ~30 tolerates a late run + a weekend gap on a daily thing. Optional 'proves' (path or glob, repo-relative) names the output that shows the task's WORK actually landed: a nonzero exit whose proof output is fresh is reported as a warning, not paged as a death. The proof must be no older than the run it claims to prove.

windows_tasks.name: TC Grocery Ad Pulls 0700
windows_tasks.why: 07:00 weekly-ad pull for every store whose ad rolled over (capture-run -Kind ad; captures only, no chain). proves = the ads file itself: a run-log exists the moment the process starts, so proving with it downgraded a killed run (0xC000013A) to 'work landed'.

windows_tasks.name: TC Grocery Daily Capture 0800
windows_tasks.why: 08:00 quarterly-rotation capture + the ONE daily chain: compare -> guards -> publish -> recipes -> commit

windows_tasks.name: TC Grocery Capture Watchdog 0930
windows_tasks.why: 10:30 outcome check of the two tasks above (was 09:30 until 2026-08-31; it now runs AFTER the 09:45 alert-triage pass, so a board triage has already unblocked and republished is not reported as a failure - see Test-RunSuperseded in capture-watchdog.ps1) (schedule, run record, board, publish, ads, browser flags) + this heartbeat. EXITS 1 BY DESIGN whenever it has findings, and it is the script that RUNS health-heartbeat - without this flag the heartbeat pages about the watchdog every day the watchdog does its job (self-referential, permanent from its first real finding).

windows_tasks.name: TC Graph Nightly Matching
windows_tasks.why: 21:30 nightly graph matching (graph/pipeline/nightly.ps1 -HardStop 06:30 -MaxMinutes 150). Registered 2026-08-22, AFTER Brad's three-task rule was written, and never added here - so from that day nothing would have noticed if it stopped: health-heartbeat flagged it as TASK UNWATCHED every morning and the drift check is what finally named it (2026-08-24). proves = its own status stamp, which the run rewrites at the end; the task can exit 0 having done nothing, the stamp cannot.

windows_tasks.name: TC Recipe Harvest Crawl
windows_tasks.why: 18:00 daily recipe candidate crawl (meal-prep/pipeline/harvest-crawl.ps1). Registered 2026-08-24 and likewise never added here. proves = the dated crawl log, which is appended on every run including one that finds no new candidates; candidate-pool.json would have been the wrong proof because a legitimately empty crawl never touches it, and a proof that only exists on a good day pages on the ordinary ones.

output_files.why: public price feed every card fetches
derived item->bid map (tools + top5 badges read it; regenerated daily)
